BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph NO. JUL 03 HON. MARVIN T, AZARCON Municipal Mayor Municipality of Lanuza Province of Surigao Del Sur Dear Hon. Azarcon: This has reference to your letter dated 22 January 2024 requesting for a legal opinion regarding the classification of land as outlined in your Zoning Ordinance (Comprehensive Land Use Plan - CLOP) and the Department of Agrarian Reform's (DAR) Conversion Order. The facts and circumstances are as follows: Recently, an applicant applied for a building permit to construct a gasoline station in the Municipality of Lanuza. The same was withheld as the present zoning ordinance of the municipality provides that the proposed construction area was classified as agricultural land. While in the process of updating the municipality's CLOP, the landowner applied for the conversion of the land from agricultural to commercial through the DAR Regional Office 13, and it consequently issued a Conversion Order of the subject area. The LGU of Lanuza maintains that the basis for land conversion should be in accordance with Sec. 4 of MC No. 54 dated June 8, 1993. Land classification and land conversion should align and complement the CLUP or zoning ordinance and not contradict each other. On the other hand, DAR contends that the land reclassification is not a prerequisite for a land conversion. In addition, such a Conversion Order is sufficient for the issuance of the locational clearance paving the way for the issuance of building permit and potentially business permit. The following issues are raised for clarification, to wit: (1) Whether a DAR Conversion Order, deviating from LGU's Land Use Plan supersede the LGU's zoning ordinance? (2) If the land classification under the zoning ordinance of the LGU (CLUP) is not a prerequisite for issuance of DAR's land conversion order? (3) If there is a conflict between the existing land classification and the Conversion Order, can the LGU issue a locational clearance based solely on the DAR's Conversion Order? "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(4) Does the land conversion take precedence over the Zoning Ordinance in the issuance of a locational clearance? It is important to delve on the distinction between conversion and reclassification. Conversion is the act of changing the current use of a piece of agricultural land into some other use as approved by the DAR while reclassification is the act of specifying how agricultural lands shall be utilized for non-agricultural uses such as residential, industrial, and commercial, as embodied in the land use plan, subject to the requirements and procedures for land use conversion. In view thereof, a mere reclassification Of an agricultural land does not automatically allow a landowner to change its use. He has to undergo the process of conversion before he is permitted to use the agricultural land for other purposesl. It is clear from the aforesaid distinction between reclassification and conversion that agricultural lands though reclassified to residential, commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural uses must still undergo the process of conversion before they can be used for the purpose to which they are intended. Nevertheless, emphasis must be given to the fact that DAR's conversion authority can only be exercised after the effectivity of Republic Act No. 6657 on 15 June 1988. The said date served as the cut-off period for automatic reclassification or rezoning of agricultural lands that no longer require any DAR conversion clearance or authority, Thereafter, reclassification of agricultural lands is already subject to DAR's conversion authority. Reclassification alone will not suffice to use the agricultural lands for other purposes. Conversion is needed to change the current use of reclassified agricultural lands2, While we take note of the fact that the CLUP is in the process of updating, we opine that the DAR Conversion Order must not deviate from the LGU's Land Use Plan. The law is clear, the DAR shall refer to the comprehensive land use plan as the main reference regarding land use conversions applications. Further the IRR of the Local Govemment Code also prescribes that such plans shall serve as the primary and dominant bases for future use of land resources and reclassification of agricultural lands. We cite Sec. 4 of the MC3 which authorizes cities and municipalities to reclassify agricultural lands into nonagricultural uses, to wit: SEC. 4. Use of the comprehensive land use plans and ordinances as primary reference documents in land use conversions. -Pursuant to RA 6657 and EO 129-A, actions on applications for land use conversions on individual landholdings shall remain as the responsibility of DAR, which shall utilize as its primary reference documents the comprehensive land use plans and accompanying ordinance passed upon and approved by the LGUs concemed, together with the National Land Use Policy. As to the second matter, we find in the negative. One of the Criteria for Conversion under Sec. 8.3.1 of DAR AO No. 1, s. 20024 is that the same must be consistent with 1 Alarcon vs. CA, 453 Phil. 373, 382-383 (2003). 2 CREBA vs. The Secretary of Agrarian Reform. G.R. No. 183409, June 18, 2010. 3 MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. PRESCRIBING THE GUIDELINES GOVERNING SECTION 20 OF RA 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AUTHORIZING CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES TO RECLASSIFY AGRICULTURAL LANDS INTO NONAGRICULTURAL USES 4 Comprehensive Rules on Land Use Conversion Page 2 of 3

the natural expansion of the municipality or locality, as contained in the approved physical framework and land use plan. Further, one of the documentary requirements to effect a land conversion under Sec. 10.15 is the Certification from the HLURB Regional Officer on the actual zoning or classification of the land subject of the application on the approved comprehensive land use plan. Hence, any land conversion order from the DAR must be consistent with the land use plan as provided under the subject AO. In case of conflict between the land classification and the conversion order and the consequent issuance of the locational clearance, we find with more reason that said clearance must not be issued. In case of disparity between the two, proper remedies may be resorted to as provided under the law. As regards the zoning ordinance, it must be established that the subject properties were classified or reclassified as residential by any authorized govemment agency prior to June 15, 1998. In the absence of such declaration, there is an inevitable conclusion that the subject property remains to be agricultural and within the coverage of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law (CARI-)5. Anent the last issue, we maintain that a zoning ordinance must prevail over a conversion order in the issuance of a locational clearance. In the same vein that a zoning ordinance is in accordance with the CLUP, the Conversion Order of the DAR must be consistent with the former, Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts, We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you.
